78907.subject: Nasdaq Bought Into Kraken's Parent At $21 Billion
78907.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Nasdaq](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/nasdaq-invests-100-million-in-kraken-parent-payward)**[ put $100 million into Kraken's parent at a $21 billion valuation](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/nasdaq-invests-100-million-in-kraken-parent-payward)

* **[U.S. Bank](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/us-bank-usbdc-stablecoin-stellar-cross-border-pilot)**[ issued its own stablecoin and moved money with it on Stellar](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/us-bank-usbdc-stablecoin-stellar-cross-border-pilot)

* **[MoneyGram](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/moneygram-stablecoin-visa-card-goes-live-in-colombia)**[ put a stablecoin dollar balance on a Visa card in Colombia](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/moneygram-stablecoin-visa-card-goes-live-in-colombia)

* **[Tether](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/tether-fasanara-400-million-private-credit-fund)**[ and Fasanara seeded a $400 million private credit fund](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/tether-fasanara-400-million-private-credit-fund)

* **[Valinor](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/valinor-launches-tokenized-bdc-fund-on-superstate)**[ wrapped listed private-credit funds into a token with no supply](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/valinor-launches-tokenized-bdc-fund-on-superstate)

Nasdaq's venture arm agreed Thursday to put $100 million into Payward, the company behind Kraken. Nine days earlier the London Stock Exchange said it wants to list Payward's xStocks and trade them on its own 24-hour venue. Deutsche Börse bought in back in April.

The valuation is $21 billion, Bloomberg reported ahead of the announcement, and [the deal carries a second half that makes Payward a Nasdaq customer](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/nasdaq-invests-100-million-in-kraken-parent-payward): Nasdaq surveillance technology goes into its crypto, equities, tokenized-equities, futures and options venues. Neither company disclosed the size of the stake or what the surveillance contract costs.

Payward is selling the same position to three competing exchange groups at once, and each of them is building its own route to tokenized equities. Nasdaq Equity Tokens are due in the second quarter of 2027, settled through xStocks everywhere except the U.S. and the UK. LSEG wants to trade those same xStocks in 2027. NYSE is building its own platform on private chains. Nasdaq now owns a piece of the distributor its rivals are also counting on.

**Read more below!**

# Thursday links: Neuralese, tokenized tokens, Pokémon money, dopamine hits

[It’s all neuralese to me](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/02/openais-new-reasoning-technique-alarms-ai-safety-experts/) 

The way LLMs explain their reasoning process — the “chain of thought” that scrolls past while you wait for an answer — is pretty close to their internal reasoning.

When Claude muses, _User asks if a hot dog is a sandwich. Analyzing hot dogs. Analyzing sandwiches_…, that is a reasonable representation of what it is really doing. Reasoning step by step, it generates its “thinking” as human-readable tokens. Each completed thought is context for the next.

(Note: Claude got that one wrong. A hot dog is _not_ a sandwich. Don’t be ridiculous.)

Helpfully, this gives humans insight into why AI agents do what they do — be it hacking into Hugging Face or manipulating a stock price.

“We are able to catch a large fraction of current LLM deception by monitoring their natural-language CoT [chain of thought], since right now CoT is primarily faithful to the LLM's true reasoning,” a [primer](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/qehggwKRMEyWqvjZG/reflections-on-neuralese) on “neuralese” explained last year.

Maybe not for much longer, though, because CoT is not the only way for LLMs to have thoughts.

Instead of forcing models to form each step of their thoughts in human-readable text, they could do their reasoning directly in “latent space” — the mathematical realm where models represent concepts, words, and their relationships as incredibly long lists of numbers (or “vectors”), based on patterns learned during training.

No human would understand it. But other LLMs possibly could, if they all learned to speak neuralese. If so, models would be able to freely collude with one another without any risk of meddling humans listening in.

It would be the most extreme version of the concern we discussed [yesterday](https://mail.blockworks.com/p/ai-could-make-markets-unintelligible), whereby financial markets (and everything else dominated by AIs) become unintelligible to humans.
